claims.text: Formation and persistence of a protective scale in CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C is mainly governed by the alloy's ability to form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer.
In CrFeCoNiAl, preferential Al oxidation can outcompete Cr oxidation and outward Cr diffusion.
Cr diffuses outward faster than oxygen diffuses inward during chromia-scale growth.
Chromia can form volatile CrO3 above 900 °C.
Al2O3 scales grow more slowly and are more stable than chromium-oxide scales.
An equimolar AlCoCrFeNi alloy forms passivating oxides containing Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
A dense, continuous alumina layer limits oxygen ingress and maintains adhesion at the metal/oxide interface.
An Al2O3 scale controls both inward oxygen transport and outward metal-cation transport.
Diffusion control by the alumina scale prevents the development of thermal stresses that cause cracking and spallation.
Oxides formed in CrFeCoNiMn or CrFeCoNiSi are less adherent or grow too rapidly compared with alumina.
CrFeCoNiAl will maintain a continuous, coherent, slow-growing Al2O3-dominated scale above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiAl will have superior high-temperature oxidation and corrosion resistance relative to CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi scales will be more prone to cracking and spallation because of volatile or poorly adherent oxides or mismatched diffusion kinetics.
Replacing Mn or Si with Al changes the concentration of the active element available to form Al2O3.
The Mn- or Si-containing baseline exhibits unstable oxide formation with cracking or spallation under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies to both single-phase and multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions.
Alloy chemistry, microstructure, surface heterogeneity, and phase instability can influence the oxide structure formed by high-entropy alloys.
The Al concentration threshold required to produce a continuous protective alumina layer remains unquantified.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as compositionally identical while simultaneously replacing Al with Mn or Si; samples with different X elements are not compositionally identical.
